notes: PARTIAL (2026-11-16, the 1985 code reads, rulings of batch 10): RECORD DELIMITER. The clause on a fixed-length file compiles with a warning only, and ANY word is taken as its implementor-name (`RECORD DELIMITER IS F1`, the file's own name, compiles) though the implementation defines none. See below: decided. Owner: kb/Work PB5844 (open). Ruled in kb/Work/PB5683/2026-11-16-rulings-code-reads-batch-10.md; the 1985 rows chained into this one: 1985-FMT-VII.2.8.2, 1985-GR-VII.2.8.4-3, 1985-GR-VII.2.8.4-5, 1985-SR-VII.2.8.3-1. The documented decline reaches only the STANDARD-1 arm of the clause (kb/Work PB5844); the part below is what the decline does cover. The prose that follows is the stored account, kept as the account of the part that holds. || "The RECORD DELIMITER clause may be specified only for variable-length records" is NOT enforced, and the licence is express rather than inferred. §4.2.6 ¶3, second sentence: "Although this warning mechanism shall identify processor-dependent elements that are not supported, it is not required to diagnose syntax errors within this unsupported syntax" (cite.py --check OK). The clause is unsupported whole — docs/CONFORMANCE.md §2 row 26 for the STANDARD-1 arm (Annex A.3 item 26) and §7 A.1 item 150 for the feature-name arm — and COBOL1778 names it at every edition, which is the obligation §4.2.6 ¶3 does impose. Enforcing SR1 anyway was considered and REJECTED as a rejects-legal-source risk, not skipped: SR1's own NOTE makes variable-length-ness partly an implementor determination (A.1 items 147-148, both still open), and §9.1.7.2 makes a LINE SEQUENTIAL file's records variable with no RECORD clause written at all, so a test keyed on FileModel.Varying would refuse legal source in order to enforce a rule the standard excuses. The golden's four files are all SR1-legal (RECORD IS VARYING), so nothing here depends on the unenforced case.
